summary.headline: Royal Orchid Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 34% to INR 116 crore and EBITDA 53% to INR 31.66 crore, helped by a Tanzania disinvestment gain.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income was INR 116 crore against INR 86.77 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA rose to INR 31.66 crore from INR 20.79 crore. Reported PAT of INR 14.73 crore was inflated by an exceptional gain on disinvesting the Tanzania subsidiary Multi Hotels Limited, while PBT before exceptional items rose to INR 5.57 crore from INR 4.43 crore. Sequentially, EBITDA fell about 3.8% on revenue up 2.7%, which management attributed to monsoon seasonality and roughly INR 1 to 1.5 crore of pre-opening costs for a Vadodara hotel. ICONIQA Mumbai reached EBITDA positive in the quarter for the first time, but bottom-line inflection remains unproven.

segments.name: Managed hotels
segments.commentary: Keys up ~7%, ARR up ~4.5% and occupancy up ~2% YoY in Q2; managed-hotel revenue up ~10-10.5%. Overall managed occupancy ~59% at ADR ~INR 4,000. PBT up ~11.5% YoY.

segments.name: ICONIQA Mumbai
segments.commentary: Opened end-September 2025 and was EBITDA positive in Q2 FY27 for the first time. Management targets INR 25 crore quarterly top line this fiscal; Q4 FY26 was INR 23 crore. Management estimates ~INR 2 crore per quarter GST input-credit disallowance hit.

segments.name: Vadodara hotel (JLO, revenue share)
segments.commentary: Newly opened in Q2 under a revenue-share model; pre-opening cost of roughly INR 1 to 1.5 crore hit the quarter's EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Managed-hotel growth expected to be above the 10-15% range from next year, and faster than 10-12% this year; management gave a 'double-digit growth' qualifier but no revenue target.
Around 30 hotels with close to 1,800 keys to open over the next ~12 months; pipeline of over 50 properties adding more than 3,500 rooms.
ICONIQA targeted to reach INR 25 crore quarterly top line in FY27, with Q4 the strongest quarter.
Other expenses expected to stay around INR 33-35 crore per quarter for the rest of the year, with no major surprises expected.
Management sees a bottom-line improvement from the second year of ICONIQA's operations; long-term goal set for 2030.
Management hopes for GST input-credit relief from the government from January onward.
capex_capacity: Opened five hotels adding 426 rooms in the last quarter; portfolio now over 127 operating hotels (177 including signed hotels).
Development pipeline of over 50 upcoming properties expected to add more than 3,500 rooms.
Growth is asset-light through partner-owned and managed structures.
Ramping up the development team to support pipeline conversion.
demand_pricing: ICONIQA occupancy was 70% in Q2 and H1 FY27, versus 81% in FY26; management cited the war-driven drop in Bombay inbound traffic in Q1 (April start) and seasonal monsoon weakness in Q1/Q2.
Marginally higher ICONIQA occupancy seen for the current quarter, with a clean run of holidays through 20 December.
Management says the market-comp annualised level is around 75% occupancy for ICONIQA, which it expects to approach.
Premiumisation strategy under way: Royal Orchid Resort Bangalore EBITDA reportedly rose from INR 80 lakh to INR 2 crore after investment.
Most managed hotels are mid-market with ADR below INR 7,500; GST input-credit disallowance on rent-linked costs is a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Managed-hotel growth trajectory and Q2 PBT margin versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said growth will be above the 10-15% range from next year, and faster than 10-12% this year, given ~30 hotels and ~1,800 keys opening over 12 months. Amit Jaiswal said managed-hotel PBT rose ~11.5% YoY with operating margin ~37-38% pre-tax, or ~36% after eliminating the 5% royalty.

qa_highlights.question: What top line gets ICONIQA to breakeven and when will it reach INR 25 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Baljee said the target is INR 25 crore quarterly top line this financial year; Q4 is strongest and last Q4 was INR 23 crore. He noted Q2 was the first EBITDA-positive quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When will the bottom line inflect, given upfront costs and asset-light ROCE goals?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the 2030 long-term goal remains, ICONIQA's second year should show bottom-line improvement, and GST disallowance is costing about INR 2 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA fall sequentially and what margin to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal attributed it to monsoon seasonality and ~INR 1-1.5 crore pre-opening cost for the Vadodara hotel, and expects a better EBITDA going forward; no margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: ICONIQA occupancy trend and ADR?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Baljee said FY26 occupancy was 81%, Q1 and Q2 FY27 were 70%, and Q2 ADR rose from ~INR 7,800 to ~INR 8,000. He argued like-for-like comparison is more relevant, and management did not give a stable ARR figure.

qa_highlights.question: Governance: qualified audit opinions, SEBI order, and promoter resolutions defeated by institutions?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the SEBI issue is partly resolved in the company's favour, one accounting issue is pending with a final hearing held and an order expected soon, and the audit matters are being defended with no financial impact expected. Arjun Baljee cited premiumisation as the path to better ARR.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and timeline of the Ksheer Sagar NCLT matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the NCLT matter is with the partner, creates no financial implication even on outcome, and is a control issue with no defined timeline given.

risks_watch: Bottom-line conversion: PBT before exceptionals only INR 5.57 crore on INR 116 crore income; reported PAT is flattered by the Tanzania disinvestment gain.
GST input-credit disallowance on lease and revenue-share costs, about INR 2 crore per quarter, with government relief hoped for from January.
ICONIQA must reach INR 25 crore quarterly revenue to make its PBT break even; Q2 was INR 20 crore.
Pending SEBI accounting order and NCLT matter with partner Ksheer Sagar; management says no financial impact but timelines are unclear.
Auditor qualifications on the last three years' accounts; management says these are outside its control.
Pipeline execution depends on partners delivering hotels on time and market conditions; no revenue targets given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and premiumisation, but defensive on profitability and governance. Management repeatedly deferred the bottom-line inflection to ICONIQA's second year and pointed to GST and seasonality, declined to give revenue targets, and answered governance questions by citing favourable SEBI outcomes and ongoing defence of audit matters.

So the company is growing very fast and in time to come, definitely a lot of good results will be shown by the company.
We are not giving revenue targets, unfortunately, because as we mentioned the last call as well, given, what's happened with the war and things like that happened this year.

tone.note: Management was confident on hotel openings, managed-hotel growth and premiumisation, but defensive on profitability, GST costs, and governance; analysts pushed on the ICONIQA breakeven path, the sequential EBITDA decline, and the SEBI and NCLT matters.

oneOffs.what: Tanzania subsidiary (Multi Hotels Ltd) disinvestment gain inflates reported PAT to INR 14.73 crore vs PBT before exceptionals of INR 5.57 crore; gain not quantified in brief
ICONIQA Mumbai Q2 FY26 base was INR 3 crore revenue and INR 1.4 crore EBITDA loss; Q2 FY27 revenue ~INR 20 crore, so the new hotel drives much of the YoY revenue growth

quality.why: Total income rose about 34% to INR 116 crore, mainly from volume (more keys, and ICONIQA Mumbai ramping from INR 3 crore to about INR 20 crore), but the brief shows a large Tanzania disinvestment gain inflating reported PAT, while PBT before exceptionals rose only about 26% (INR 4.43 to 5.57 crore) and managed-hotel PBT grew about 11.5%.
